question: Allopurinol (a xanthine oxidase inhibitor) should be initiated during an acute gout attack to rapidly lower uric acid and shorten the duration of the flare.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Initiating allopurinol during acute gout WORSENS the attack by mobilising urate crystals. The acute attack should first be managed with colchicine, NSAIDs, or corticosteroids. Allopurinol is started 2–4 weeks after complete resolution, with prophylactic colchicine co-prescribed for 3–6 months.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is FALSE. Starting allopurinol during an acute attack mobilises urate deposits and can prolong or worsen the flare. Allopurinol should be started 2–4 weeks after the acute attack has fully resolved, with concomitant low-dose colchicine or NSAID prophylaxis for at least 3–6 months.
